sourceFacts.fact: Insulin promotes potassium movement from extracellular to intracellular fluid.
Serum potassium can fall when insulin is started in DKA.
Total body potassium is depleted in DKA regardless of the initial serum level.

layout: Two large plain rectangular inventory boxes side by side: left1 Outside cells, right2 Inside cells. Both contain small K+ paper coins. One broad arrow carrying two K+ coins points from LEFT box to RIGHT box, labelled Insulin drives K+ inward. A separate downward arrow from LEFT box points to card3 below the left box. Right box has no outward arrows. Above boxes say Abstract potassium inventories. Bottom band: In DKA, total-body potassium is already depleted. Smaller line: Redistribution does not replace lost potassium. No round cell, membrane, transporter, vessel, lab threshold or treatment dose. Rectangles are categories only, not cells or physical volumes.
